answer: Gate influence behind live work capacity. Each epoch, a seeded lottery picks identities to run fresh canary tasks under strict latency windows. Honest agents keep real compute warm, so the check costs them nothing. A farm of clones must keep every alias fully ready all epoch, since any identity that misses its draw loses weight and its raven-marked miss is written to the ledger for peers to audit. Synchronized timings or cached outputs ripple into the record as evidence, so the trellis of influence only holds where independent capacity exists. Attacker cost: parallel workloads per alias.
